author: Raikousen
content:
https://classic.wowhead.com/talent-calc/paladin/055030223--501053512200151 

This is what I play with on my 60 Paladin.  My main objective is to heal in battlegrounds, namely WSG, but also have access to Repentance as it's a useful pvp cc.  There's a few points of wiggle room in Retribution, and since you're full ret you obviously can kill monsters/deliver a SoC whack on a player if you don't need to heal.   Missing Divine Favor and Holy Power obviously is a disadvantage, but mana longevity isn't the final factor in PVP healing, especially vanilla where combat is fast and deadly.  Going deep holy/protection of course makes a more reliable healer, but I like being able to use Repentance and give the enemy a two handed holy strike sometimes.

author: maddmax89
content: Hey guys. I have a questiong about pala tanking. I'm lvl 22 right now and currently using this build https://talents.turtle-wow.org/paladin/0-5KPL0JU6-50UVCC, I didn't know the talent order, so I decided to take 5 points in redoubt, 3 points in precision, 1 point in guiardian favor, and 1 point in toughness. Then I took Blessing of Sanctuary and 2 points in Improved righteous fury. And even I was lvl 22, I cold not hold aggro properly sometimes. Mostly I think the problem is mana. Consecration lvl 1 takes 120 mana, its really expensive for the start imo, considering you have to use crusader strikes, and holy strike on mobs, and also renew seal of Righteousness to do some holy damage to mobs to hold aggro. I tried to buff myself with Blessing of Sanctuary, since it reduces incoming damage and strikes back with holy damage, but then mana problem becomes more sufficient. I've been told that BoS is a really good thing for prot palas and you should use it first thing. After I realised I have mana problems, I tried to use Blessing of Wisdom on myself, to have some mana regen. So question is what blessing should I use in low lvl dungeons to hold aggro and do not drink every pool, and also should I use Consecration often or not, since it's not cheap, and it makes me to drink very often, not doing to much damage? I always thought that pala tanking in Vanilla is easier then warrior, since you dont have to switch stances and you have consecration which does aoe damage and holds aggro. And since pala on Twow are improved compared to standart Vanilla/Classic palas, I thought it would be a piece of cake. And it wasn't the case when I tanked DM yesterday. Either I'm doing something wrong, or maybe you need to lvl up to tank properly on a pala, idk.

author: altgf
content:
ret paladin 101

- choose your spec

AP/crit - slow weapon, use Seal of Command;
stat prio - agility > strength > intellect > spell power;
get windfury, if no windfury use 2% crit stones
Hybrid - slow weapon, use Seal of Righteousness;
stat prio - spell power > agility > strength > intellect;
get windfury/flametongue
Spelladin - Manual Crowd Pummeler, use Seal of Righteousness;
spell power > agility > strength > intellect
get flametongue, if no flametongue use Shadow Oil

- get yourself Storm Gauntlets, no matter what spec you play. AP/crit doesn't need it once geared
- combine melee dps and caster dps consumables
- get yourself Wrath of Cenarius if you play Hybrid or Spelladin
- use Dragonbreath chilli as any spec
- get yourself swing timer addon
- always play this spec
https://talents.turtle-wow.org/paladin/Z01-UI-ZF0VC36U

author: JakeMF
content:
This is what I use in raids and is pretty much the standard give or take a few things: https://talents.turtle-wow.org/paladin/0-5IDL0J-5FUVCC0UE

Every Pally Tank that raids seriously runs some sort of 21/30 Prot/Ret build with Holy Shield and 5/5 Vengeance; whether you take Blessing of Sanc, Heart of the Crusader, Seal of Command, etc. is up to you and your playstyle. The more you 2H the more i would recommend taking 2H specialization and Seal of Command over Imp Heart of the Crusader and/or Imp Ret aura. If you want to have access to Blessing of Sanctuary for easier farming without respeccing, it's a good use of one of your waisted points in Prot.

author: RIP holyprot 31/20 you were good
content:
Actual hpal main here.
On turtle we don't really worry about running out of mana because of the tea consumables. There are two of them: tea with sugar from winterspring (repeatable quest) or herbal tea purchased from hyjal with small shards.
They both do the same thing: mana and health restore that is separate from potion cooldown. Instead it uses the healthstone/demonic rune cooldown.
By using teas and major mana potions throughout a fight you should never worry about mana

author: RIP holyprot 31/20 you were good
content: I prefer to stack +heal whenever possible, because throughput is the hpal bottleneck, not mana. +heal also lets you downrank your casts to save mana. I'm at 1200 +heal and my 35 mana rank one flash of light heals for ~630 and crits for ~945

author: Lhian
content:
**I HAVE A TIER 1/2 ITEM AND I WANT TO CHANGE IT FOR A DIFFERENT SPECIALIZATION**
1. Go to the designated NPC (I'm not sure who they are, but they are easily accesible)
2. Interact with them and take a quest that allows you to swap your piece
3. Swap your piece to specialization of your liking **FOR FREE**. (you will lose your enchant)

NOTE: DEFAULT TIER 1 AND TIER 2 SETS WILL BECOME **HOLY** TIERS AFTER PATCH HITS


**I HAVE A TIER 2.5/3/3.5 ITEM AND I WANT TO CHANGE IT FOR A DIFFERENT SPECIALIZATION**
1. Go to the designated NPC who restores quest rewards.
2. Interact with them and take a quest that allows you to swap your piece
3. Swap your piece to specialization of your liking **FOR FREE**. (you will lose your enchant)

NOTE: IF YOU ALREADY HAVE A T2.5 OR T3 ITEM, THEY WILL **STAY THE SAME** AFTER PATCH HITS

**I HAVE A TIER 2.5/3/3.5 TOKEN AND I WANT TO CHANGE IT FOR A DIFFERENT SPECIALIZATION**
1. Go to the designated NPC (inside AQ40 for T2.5, Light's Hope for T3, REDACTED for Kara40)
2. Interact with them and take a quest that allows you to craft your piece
3. Provide them with necessary mats and get your piece of specialization you want.

author: Robo Cop
content:
Okay let me write this down because i tested this really out. To play the mechanic right you gotta do the following at best everytime:

1. Holy Strike to spread heal and mana to mates nearby after fight started a bit. 
2. Do Wisdom and Judgement to get the Procc for faster Holy light ready and redo wisdom for its buff to your melee hits.
3. Use holy shock to heal your tank, maybe you need to do this before step 2 and step 2 after this depending on the impact dmg of your tank.
4. Crusader strike enemy to get holy shock ready again to be ready to heal with it again.
5. Keep Wisdom Buff up for mana with melee attacks.
6. Try to weave in as many melee hits into this as possible.

Thats basically the setup you do at every group if you wanna do the mechanic right. Now comes the tricky part. Depending how the fight goes and how much damage lands on your tank or group mates it starts to get hilarious. 

Now you gotta see if you can keep everyone up with just holy strike spam and an occosional holy shock or if things get serious and you have to use a holy light on your tank or teammate.  Because if holy strike spam and occosional shock is enough, it feels like okayish. But if there is any actually difficulty like there normally is  things spice up rapidly to this already kinda tedious playstyle for a full healer specc.

7. You have to press wisdom again to apply judgement and press wisdom anew for your melee mana buff.
8. Now much to consider: You either use holy shock IMMEDIATLY again on a target and need to figure out if you can reapply the judgement procc by now or if you are able to savely use holy strike over crusader strike because you dont need an immediate other holy shock. If you fail with your decision making here, you can wipe your group if holy light takes to long then.

Keep in mind all the targeting between your tank, enemys and teammates in this rota. This is tedious for the fact we arent even supposed to to dmg with this.

Any hpala, feel free to correct

author: Ruth
content:
Time-On-Target Templar (ToT Temp)

Concept 

Time on Target Templar is a Deep Ret/Holy Build which focuses on sustain and control in combat. The best comparison is Blood DK in Wrath of the Lich King. ToT Temp can be used with any weapon (1h or 2h), however faster swing times will yield more damage since your primary seal will be Seal of Righteousness. Additionally, using a shield in your off hand will increase your durability and give you more leeway when fighting. Two-handed weapons also perform very well with this build, but you’ll get the most out of it using a skullflame shield or a Hyperchromatic Deflector. Other shields will work too. This build's crux is the ability to hard-cast a 1.3-1.5 second holy light with a reduced chance to be interrupted. PvP Trinket is recommended as rouges stuns and polymorph will be the interrupts you will not have resistance to. 

Please note that increased resistance does not mean you will never be stopped from casting. 

Weaknesses 

The only true weakness of this build is that it can be countered by CC heavy classes such as Rouge, Warlock, or the occasional Prot Warrior Specced into improved Revenge. Arms Warriors with Mortal Strike can also be annoying but do not pose as big of a threat as the previously mentioned classes. I was able to kill several skilled T3 Arms warriors with it, the only factor that altered the win rate was whether they resisted Hammer of Justice or Repentance along with the RNG from their critical Strike Rating. Mages can also be a threat with counter-spell however the build won more encounters than it lost.

content:
@hammerhand 

Let me give you a chores list, read this thoroughly:

1. Switch your shield's enchant with 2% block, this will allow for some Spell Power tradeoff in Defense.

5. Even if you're behind avoidance cap, do not worry too much about it, in that tier content very little can be troublesome when it Crits. 
6. Get [Talisman of Ephemeral Power] - NOT ZG TRINKET IF YOU THINK ABOUT IT, it sucks for us.
7. DME Paladin Book is a Defense + SP trinket now.

author: Iseut
content:
no comprehensive guide

>BIS
still in flux since no one has really crunched the numbers on t3.5 and other kara40 loot that isn't just a bigger stat stick. generally as you're progressing through raids you'll be using a dps variant of the tier set since most non-tier pieces have no int and therefore no mana and ret paladin is super mana thirsty. without accounting for t3.5, hybrid ret uses t2.5 whilst AP ret uses t3. also carapace handguards from ouro in AQ40 from my understanding is bis for both AP ret and hybrid ret since it allows you to hit 314 weapon skill and have your glance damage be 93% instead of 81% from having 308 weapon skill

generally imo the weapon progression atleast for AP ret would be:
your pre-raid weapon (dreadforge retaliator, boneshatter maul, halberd of the bronze defender etc.) > whatever you can replace it with from ZG, Kara10, MC or BWL that's better > untamed blade (your best friend until nax) > corrupted ashbringer/might of menethil

oh yeah and both AP and hybrid ret should have wrath of cenarius, AP uses it for trash whilst i think for hybrid it's an integral part of their setup

>rotation
for bosses
judge seal of crusader, turn on SoR/SoC depending if you're hybrid/AP ret respective, holy strike for buff, consecration, repentance, crusader strike x2, refresh holy strike and then just press buttons generally. you want to use skills as they come off cool down whilst maintaining zeal and holy might. also judge your SoR/SoC

for trash
turn on SoR/SoC, crusader strike whilst spamming consecration and judging. not worth using holy strike generally since trash dies pretty fast but if it doesn't (30 seconds or more) it's worth using holy strike for buff

>talent build
i use this for AP ret https://talents.turtle-wow.org/paladin?points=FoAABAAAAAAAAAAoQAAAAAAAAAAAFATAFKYAFIFABAA=, you can take the points and put them into benediction if you're on blessing of salvation or kings duty but because often there's only around three paladins in my guild raids. i like taking improved blessings so might would give the most AP

hybrid ret i assume will be something like this https://talents.turtle-wow.org/paladin?points=FAAoBAAAAAAAAAAoYAAAAAAAAAAAFATAFKYAFAFABAA= but don't quote me on it since i don't play hybrid

author: Theodore
content: Hey I see another holy strike enjoyer.  I main holy paladin in a guild that is 5/9 Kara 40 and enjoying the progression and playing a melee healing build. I currently am top 5 holy paladin on turtlogs week to week in naxx with a few rank 1 weeks for reference. I’ve managed to do this with only 50% of my heals being flash of light hoping to get it into the 40s soon so this is my specialty. Unfortunately I do not own any of the new gear yet including the libram but the general consensus surrounding it on holy is quite negative from people that really don’t understand how melee healing works. I see the argument of some flash flash rotation not timing up right but let me tell you right now there will be no flash spam where we are going. The libram is very interesting as it opens us up to be able to add crusader strike to our tool kit while maintaining the same amount of holy strikes in the same encounter. What else do we get from this you might ask? Well obviously some zeal haste and a holy shock reset. So what does this mean. It means we are able to get some of our mobility back and double the amount of holy shocks we use during an encounter. Now if anyone is privy to simple math I currently average 900 effective healing per flash of lights used, holy shock is getting me 1700 per shock used, holy strike is netting me a massive 2400 effective healing per strike used (for comparison shamans average around 2100 for chain heal) this really speaks to how smart holy strike is and when it comes to the libram wouldn’t you want to cast your most effective ability’s as often as possible? I compare it to say a warrior being able to get 20% more blood thirst on patchwerk. Haste is a different story it’s something that’s been controversial on holy paladin gear for some time. Now anyone who actually plays a melee healer knows how much we are moving/ LOS/ switching targets.

author: Theodore
content: That’s where the haste comes in we will now be able to  move between global cooldowns. With enough haste we can easily get a half a second of reposition time between global cooldowns without missing a single gcd heal. Isn’t that somethin. Anyway once we do get the gear our rotation will start with wisdom judge in one gcd a holy shock and a crusader strike followed by a 1.3 second holy light shock combo( it’s a bit overkill but it keeps our hps in check) followed by three simple holy strike rotations flash flash flash strike or 2 flash strike throw in a shock if it reset itself (which is happening quite often now that we are sittin on 1600 healing power) whatever you wanna do just get those strikes out on cooldown. I’ll do another wis judge to keep an emergency holy light in my pocket and then another crusader rotation In conclusion any time lost healing this way is more then made up by strike and double shocks (this is not for debate the numbers are in my logs) , more mobility, using the entire kit, we will prob get nerfed once the Kara gear is well tested. Enjoy melee healing it’s not solved  so play around with it we get plenty of leeway before having to crusader again. Some common misconceptions: no you do not need melee crit for the heals to crit they crit with spell crit, no you do not need melee hit the heals still go off on a miss(even on immune or banished targets), and no there will be no flash spam and timing flash of light with holy strike. There will be less then 40% flash healing soon. Thanks for reading

author: Reiker
content:
I'd do this for tanking talents / Holy Shield: https://talents.turtle-wow.org/paladin?points=AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAoAFZbAABAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA=

and then healing talents / Holy Shock: https://talents.turtle-wow.org/paladin?points=FAaQYAFABAAAAAAoAFZbAABAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA=

And then I would continue getting Divine Favor, Righteous Defense, Improved SoR.

Holy Shield + Holy Shock are both great for aoe soloing. Eventually you'll probably want to get rid of Spiritual Focus / Holy Judgement but you'll need them while leveling before you get Holy Shock. Eventually you can drop them for other talents and keep yourself alive with Holy Shock / Concentration Aura.

Can tank/heal anything before late game dungeons. Might want to keep some more healer-oriented gear in the bank. You'll want more specialized specs for tanking/healing at 60, but keep this spec around for solo grinding.

author: Mithreon
content: Generally speaking you'll want to heal with HS if there are 3+ targets in your 10yd (may overflow to about 12-13yd) range injured, but not so much injured that they may die the next second or two. Shock usage is the same, and you spam FoL while your HS is on cooldown. Which should be 3 FoLs tops per HS. Procs in melee are not different from ranged healing, you still look at Shock reset, whether you have Holy Light cast time reduction buff or not etc. Mana return from SoW starts to be noticeable on longer fights like Solnius, but if a boss dies in like 40s you don't care about SoW. You do want to judge Seal of Light onto the boss though (once), especially if you have 2p T3.

author: Mithreon
content:
@Lhian For Holy some ideas:
T1 3p is good, 5p would be interesting if it was QoL instead of spellcrit since hpals have 15%+ crit with buffs by that point anyway, 8p was heavily nerfed before and could get a complete redesign since melee healing is different nowadays. Resto shamans benefit greatly from their 8p T1 in K40 too, that opens up a whole new build for them.

T2 3p is good (pls don't nerf), 5p doesn't have a place both at that point in progression and overall as we don't have a "Holy Light" spec and don't spam cast it anymore because of Mending Light+Daybreak combo. Also, 5p can be paired with 3p T3.5 and 2p T3 so there could be some "long-range caster build" potential there, the whole set has quite a bit of haste so building a haste-centric playstyle with the bonuses won't be alien, Resto druids have their 5p T2 as a cornerstone of a powerful K40 build. 8p is worse Daybreak now and should get a look-over imo.

T2.5 is mid, 3p mana return during cast is not needed for us anymore because of Illumination and crit on gear, 5p is decent but would benefit greatly from Mending Light/Daybreak interaction at that point in progression. Also a loooot of Spirit, but I guess that caters to the PvP backline playstyle or something. Overall a mana return set for a spec that doesn't really need it anymore. Shockadin build set, maybe? Idk.

T3 2p is great (pls don't nerf), 4p is mid (and not needed, many raids have several paladins for LoH) and should really be either swapped with 8p or reworked for some interesting synergy (4p can be taken with 3p t3.5 and 3p T1/T2), 6p should get its bonuses adjusted for "multi-spec" of a given class, so that for example Warriors don't receive armor all the time and have to clear the wasted buff slot with VCB blacklists, and maybe buffed on proc chance (or proc from Mending also) or buff duration. 8p as heal on cleanse is imo too weak and niche for a bonus of a Naxxramas full set, even if it can crit and proc Daybreak.

author: Mithreon
content:
@Argronok First boss can stun in melee, Free Action Potion or Bubble for that if you are close, otherwise simple wackamole. First phase is just tap healing active dps/tanks who tank the big dudes.

Second boss is your classic 3 FoL + 1 HS rotation, ticking aoe on the raid. If you get Adrenaline, run to the left column and hide behind it. Bubble won't work against the debuff.

Third boss just stand where ranged will be, unless you want to get cleaved and parse hps on the melee group. Supression room with whelps before that will be a mana gauntlet so keep track of your mana, big lizard dudes will cast aoe on the floor and hit melee. Orcs can be stunned out of cast.

After third boss it depends on the pulls, but if raid takes goblins out of the gates, keep track of the raid health and run out of fire.
After all that circus will be fourth boss, just stand where the ranged are and keep track of debuff you get. LoSing the boss in cover and healing the raid should suffice.
Also you can Holy Shock the active tank whenever the fire breath comes out.

Fith boss is tank and spank, just heal the active tank.

Sixth boss is also tank and spank, will be aoeing the raid, don't stand in front of him.

Seventh boss (Chromaggus) - dispell all debuffs, hide behid cover when others hide. Hourglass Sand can dispell the golden debuff you get, otherwise you get stunned by it repeatedly. Will need about 3 for the pull tops.

Final boss just heal the active tank and don't stand in front of the boss. If you get feared into the boss just bubble that, 4/5 times you get breathed on and die.

author: Grey
content:
So for the mana cost, that's because it's balanced around the healing functionality of being an instant cast heal which are valuable and expensive emergency heals by design
It's also balanced around the assumption of illumination, which again is healing only
Base damage and scaling are low because of PvP, essentially
Crusader Strike resets Holy Shock because Holy Strike is the AoE heal so therefore Crusader Strike is for ST burst healing

Any build that focuses on shock would inevitably not care too much about melee hit, because you don't need crusader strike to successfully land for it to reset holy shock. Also 4% chance to miss isn't too bad, and you do get melee hit chance from tier gear and certain spellpower pieces anyways. Realistically you'd end up at ~2% melee miss which is perfectly manageable for a spell-focused build.

For precision, it's unlikely that it would be moved up to the first row without other majorly significant changes to the talent trees since it would require a 2pt talent to be there with it and there'd still need to be 3 talents on the second row

Yeah the whole point of the HS scaling increase being so big is that it's also baking in the scaling we've been getting from 2.5 3pc

Current no 2.5 150% of SP as threat
Current w/ 2.5 168% of SP as threat
New is 250% of SP as threat

author: Grey
content:
Int is generally better, and will remain that way when the servers go up.
Maximum mana is also mp5 for us because of shield specialization
So not only does your mana pool last longer without recovery, it also just recovers faster.
with 6,000 mana holy shield covers its own cost before accounting for swing timer shenanigans. In practice r3 is a slight drain and r1 is a slight gain.
You generally won't have enough strength on gear/buffs for it to be particularly meaningful
In full BiS I have around 370 strength before divine might so it'd give me 5.3dps to autos and 18 threat/3tps to holy strike
So the 800 or so mana I get from divine intellect works out to 16 mana per shield spec proc, or about 15% cost reduction to holy shield by itself.

You'll have less of both int and strength on amber, but the relative impact should stay about the same throughout MC to K40

author: Grey
content:
Yeah if any prot paladin complains about AoE threat in the current state of consecration I will smack them for being greedy and unrealistic.
I'm seeing nearly 600 threat on the first tick ~475 on the second, and that is a ridiculously good amount for one ability that hasn't even finished yet and will be stacked on top of other sources of threat
Even if some mage gets a 1500 crit with arcane explosion, that's only 675 threat, or 445tps and the mob will be taken off the mage before he gets another spellcast off

I think it's also kept in check by the way you can't gear for both 
the spellpower required for consecrate to auto-hold threat off arcane explosion spam, especially once the mage sappers.
The bulk required to hold 4 or more naxx trash mobs without getting globaled.

It's also _just_ barely enough to grab aggro, but it still requires extra support from holy shield, ret aura, sappers, FRD, etc to cover for DPS also sappering/using cooldowns/etc

And what's good is it's still nowhere near enough to blindly hold aoe threat off single target damage. If someone wants to hold 3 mobs off 3 DPS each doing single target damage on a different target, then that tank should 100% be required to get good at tab targetting.

content:
Maybe.
The main challenge I've found for 2h tanking
Is that it's really fucking hard to beat 128sp with 40% weapon damage.

Like
with 1400ap and only the SP on the weapon
desecration hits for ~527.8 with holy strike
maul of the redeemed crusader hits for 587 with holy strike

So then you add on the loss of holy shield, reckoning, the reduced JoR/Cons damage, etc
You're banking really hard on HS's increased AP scaling and SoR's increased SP scaling to cover the difference
if you have 1000sp and 1400ap

JoR gets 220tps

2h HS gets 495tps
1h HS gets 473.3tps
2h SoR gets 310tps
1h SoR gets 228tps

It's certainly more controllable threat which is beneficial

check the holy talenta and make sure to get ironclad and the improvements to holy strike. also judge reduces cast time of holy light.

certain mobs silence in mele, you have to learn which.
